topic: parsing is not approval: an invoice amount needs a source link and a human exception step
audience_job: decide, before selling invoice automation, what has to be traceable and human-approved
experiment_variable: opening line: JSON extraction versus approval
label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS

parts:
An invoice-to-JSON demo isn't an accounts-payable product.

Docling parses PDF tables with provenance. Activepieces supports approvals.

The service to test: link each amount to its source, flag mismatches, and leave a review trail.

https://github.com/docling-project/docling

image_brief: Editorial diagram titled 'Parsing is not approval': an invoice flows into source-linked fields and then into human review of exceptions. A proposal, not a tested integration.
alt_text: Minimal editorial diagram titled 'Parsing is not approval.' An original invoice flows into traceable source-linked fields and then human review of exceptions. This is a proposed Docling and Activepieces workflow, not a tested integration.

source_angles.thesis: Financial process value depends on traceable source evidence plus an explicit exception and approval step.
source_angles.evidence: Docling's structured document provenance and Activepieces' approval workflow; the proposed process connects them.
source_angles.counterexample: No actual integration or invoice accuracy test has been done.

source_angles.thesis: A perfect-looking JSON response may hide a false amount unless it is linked to its PDF position.
source_angles.evidence: DoclingDocument provenance and geometry can support traceability.
source_angles.counterexample: Source coordinates alone do not verify the amount or the payment authority.

source_angles.thesis: A buyer might prefer paying for fewer unresolved invoice disputes rather than for PDF conversion alone.
source_angles.evidence: Possible delivery is a reviewed queue with audit logs, not a proven commercial product.
source_angles.counterexample: No customer commitment, cost model or willingness-to-pay validation yet.
